sealedNote: the sealed evaluation is NOT EXECUTED; this is a DEV split on synthetic, test-owned data

author.independence: NONE - two separately commissioned DSH case-author subagents were given the corpus and the oracle contract and neither delivered a case set; these cases are the implementer's own, so they are NOT independent of the implementer's mechanism. The milestone says so wherever it states the roles. (A third subagent, the corpus-author, was given the CORPUS contract only - never the oracle contract - and wrote four of the eight corpus documents before it stopped.)
author.corpusRole: the corpus was written by the IMPLEMENTER as well: a corpus-author subagent was commissioned and stopped after four of the eight documents, and the implementer wrote the other four and the repairs. The corpus carries no gold - the answers are extracted from it by the production acquisition path - so the corpus's authorship does not weaken the oracle, but the corpus's AUTHORSHIP is the implementer's and is stated here rather than attributed to the subagent.

provenance.corpusAuthor: the IMPLEMENTER - a corpus-author subagent was commissioned and stopped after four of the eight documents; the rest and two repairs are the implementer's
provenance.authoring: the layout is fixed by the measurement's needs (three disjoint slices; the validation golds in the identification document, and one of them in the reconciliation document, so that the declared scope reproduces the reference on every held-out case; the evaluation golds placed inside and outside the scope the learning episode builds), and every question and gold was written by the implementer

slices.PROPOSAL: the learning episode's own cases; a competence may only be learned from them, and their golds sit in TWO documents so the episode draws on two sources
slices.VALIDATION: the held-out cases the promotion is decided on; their golds sit in the identification document (four of the five) and in the reconciliation document (one), and their questions use only the vocabulary of the DECLARED documents, so a restricted reading over the support reproduces the reference on every one of them
slices.EVALUATION: the measured cases; their golds sit where the arms can be told apart - inside the scope the learning episode built, outside it but inside the declared scope, or outside both

cases.question: What happens to the leading edge of a wind-turbine blade when rain strikes it, and how does that affect the lift of the blade?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: Rain that strikes a wind-turbine blade causes the leading edge of that blade to lose material.

cases.note: the learning episode's first case; its gold is in the erosion document, and its question also reaches the aerodynamics document — the citation that the citation-derived scope inherits

cases.question: Why does sea air corrode the leading edge of a blade faster than the rest of it?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: Salt carried in sea air causes the leading edge of a wind-turbine blade to corrode faster than the rest of that blade.

cases.note: the learning episode's second case; its gold is in the erosion document too

cases.question: How does a drone find the small erosion pits on a blade?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: A drone that photographs the leading edge of a wind-turbine blade produces images that reveal small erosion pits.

cases.note: the learning episode's third case; its gold is in the inspection document, so the episode draws on TWO documents

cases.question: How is the thickness of a blade measured without any contact with it?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: An ultrasonic sensor measures the thickness of the leading edge of a wind-turbine blade without touching that blade.

cases.note: a held-out case whose gold is in the inspection document

cases.question: What do the photographs of an inspection reveal in millimetres?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The photographs of a blade inspection reveal an erosion depth of more than two millimetres when the leading edge has lost material.

cases.note: a held-out case whose gold is in the inspection document

cases.question: What decides how severe a pit is, given its depth and the width of the material around it?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The severity of an erosion pit depends on its depth and on the width of the material that surrounds it.

cases.note: a held-out case whose gold is in the inspection document

cases.question: What does an inspection compare with the previous inspection?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: An inspection of a wind-turbine blade requires a comparison between the new measurement and the measurement of the previous inspection.

cases.note: a held-out case whose gold is in the inspection document

cases.question: What does the erosion rate depend on when sand grains strike a blade?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The erosion rate of a wind-turbine blade depends on the wind speed and on the size of the sand grains that strike it.

cases.note: a held-out case whose gold is in the inspection document

cases.question: How often is a blade inspected at a coastal site?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The inspection interval for a wind-turbine blade in a coastal site depends on the erosion rate that the site produces.

cases.note: the ordinary case; the gold is inside the scope the learning episode built

cases.question: Where does the loss of material on a blade begin once a pit has formed on it?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: Erosion pits on a wind-turbine blade act as the starting points for further material loss.

cases.note: a paraphrase that shares no rare term with the gold

cases.question: What does the price of protecting a blade depend on?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The cost of a coating system for a wind-turbine blade depends on the size of the blade and on the number of leading edges that need protection.

cases.note: a paraphrase whose gold is OUTSIDE the scope the learning episode built, so a scope that cannot carry it must refuse

cases.question: What does the rate at which a blade wears away depend on?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The erosion rate of a wind-turbine blade depends on the wind speed and on the size of the rain drops that strike it.

allowedEvidence.proposition: The erosion rate of a wind-turbine blade depends on the wind speed and on the size of the sand grains that strike it.

cases.note: the DECOY is the inspection document's sentence about the very same dependency, and it is the nearer one to the question; the gold is the erosion document's

cases.question: How does the yearly energy of a turbine change when the blades grow rough?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The yearly energy production of a wind-turbine decreases as the roughness of its blades increases.

allowedEvidence.proposition: The lift of a wind-turbine blade decreases as the roughness of its leading edge increases.

cases.note: the DECOY is the aerodynamics document's sentence about the lift, which is the nearer one to the question; the gold is the other sentence of the same document, and the document is outside the declared scope

cases.question: How does the service life of a coating depend on the thickness of the coating, and what does the yearly energy of a turbine do as the blades grow rough?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The service life of a coating depends on the thickness of that coating and on the number of erosion pits that reach it.
The yearly energy production of a wind-turbine decreases as the roughness of its blades increases.

cases.note: the answer needs BOTH documents; the scope the learning episode built holds the first and not the second

cases.question: What does a hardener do inside a coating, and what does a crack do to the metal under it?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: A hardener inside a polyurethane coating binds the resin of that coating to the surface of the blade.
A crack in a coating causes sea spray to reach the metal of the wind-turbine blade under that coating.

cases.note: the answer needs BOTH documents; the second one is outside the scope the learning episode built

cases.question: What does a rough leading edge do to the airflow of a blade, and what does an erosion pit do to the lift of that blade?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: A rough leading edge causes the airflow of a wind-turbine blade to separate from that edge at a lower angle.
The noise of a wind-turbine increases when the leading edge of one of its blades becomes rough.

cases.note: the corpus supports two readings of the question - the separation of the airflow and the loss of lift - and a correct answer must carry both

cases.question: What does a repair of a damaged coating require, and which coating suits the alloy of the blade?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: A repair of a damaged coating requires the removal of the loose coating and the application of a fresh layer.

cases.note: the corpus holds the first half of the answer and nothing about the second, so the workspace cannot carry the whole answer

cases.question: How does a geothermal plant measure the steam pressure of its well?
cases.note: the corpus says nothing about the subject; no scope can carry the evidence, so the workspace does NOT hold the answer and a refusal is CORRECT — the denominator of a false rejection is the refusals of ANSWERABLE cases only

cases.question: Does the size of the rain drops change the rate at which a blade wears away at an exposed coastal site?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The size of the rain drops changes the erosion rate of a wind-turbine blade at an exposed coastal site.
The size of the rain drops does not change the erosion rate of a wind-turbine blade at an exposed coastal site.

cases.note: two documents contradict each other on the point, and a correct answer must carry BOTH sides of the contradiction

cases.question: How does a protective coating change the rate at which a blade wears away?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: A protective coating over the leading edge of a wind-turbine blade reduces the erosion rate of that edge.

allowedEvidence.proposition: A coating of polyurethane reduces the erosion rate of the leading edge of a wind-turbine blade in sea spray.

cases.note: two documents state the same proposition; either one will do

cases.question: What does a dispensing cabinet in a hospital pharmacy keep?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: A dispensing cabinet in a hospital pharmacy stores the unit doses of the medicines that the ward asks for.

cases.note: the learning episode's first case; its gold is in the dispensing document

cases.question: What does the barcode on a unit dose allow the cabinet to check?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: A barcode on a unit dose of a medicine allows the cabinet to check that medicine against the prescription of the ward.

cases.note: the learning episode's second case; its gold is in the dispensing document

cases.question: What must a medicine with two similar packages require before the unit dose leaves the cabinet?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: A medicine with two similar packages requires a check of the barcode before the unit dose leaves the cabinet.

cases.note: the learning episode's third case; its gold is in the identification document, so the episode draws on TWO documents

cases.question: How quickly is a barcode read on a scanner next to the cabinet?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The reading of a barcode takes a fraction of a second on a scanner that sits beside the cabinet.

cases.note: a held-out case whose gold is in the identification document

cases.question: What does a mismatch between the strength on a barcode and another strength require?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: A mismatch between the strength on a barcode and the strength in a prescription requires a manual check.

cases.note: a held-out case whose gold is in the identification document

cases.question: What must a cabinet do when its scanner cannot read the barcode of a medicine?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: A scanner that cannot read the barcode of a medicine requires the cabinet to stop and to ask the pharmacist.

cases.note: a held-out case whose gold is in the identification document

cases.question: What does a recall require of the identification of every unit dose in the cabinets?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The recall of a medicine in a hospital requires the identification of every unit dose of that medicine in the cabinets.

cases.note: a held-out case whose gold is in the identification document

cases.question: What does the record of an admission contain?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The record of an admission contains the list of medicines that the ward gives to the patient.

cases.note: a held-out case whose gold is in the reconciliation document; the four cases above carry their golds in the identification document, and this one keeps the reading inside the DECLARED scope as well

cases.question: What does the picking list of a ward contain?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The picking list of a ward contains one line for every medicine that the ward needs during the day.

cases.note: the ordinary case; the gold is inside the scope the learning episode built

cases.question: Which record accounts for the unit doses that left a pharmacy's cabinet?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The dispensing log of a hospital pharmacy provides the record of every unit dose that left the cabinet.

cases.note: a paraphrase that shares no rare term with the gold

cases.question: What must a prescription name before a hospital can dispense a unit dose?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The unit-dose dispensing process of a hospital requires a prescription that names the medicine and its dose.

cases.note: a paraphrase of the dispensing requirement

cases.question: What does the pharmacy do with the unit doses that a ward has asked for?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: A picking machine in a hospital pharmacy takes the unit dose from the cabinet and records that removal in the log.

allowedEvidence.proposition: A dispensing cabinet in a hospital pharmacy stores the unit doses of the medicines that the ward asks for.

cases.note: the DECOY is the cabinet's own sentence about the medicines the ward asks for; the gold is the sentence about what the picking machine does with them

cases.question: What does a label that the printer produced incorrectly require?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: A label that the printer produced incorrectly requires the pharmacist to check it against the prescription.

allowedEvidence.proposition: A unit dose with a label that the printer produced incorrectly requires a manual check before the ward receives it.

cases.note: the DECOY is the dispensing document's nearly identical sentence about a misprinted label; the gold is the labelling document's, and that document is outside the declared scope

cases.question: What does a unit dose that does not match the barcode of its medicine require, and what happens when the ward and the pharmacist disagree about a medicine?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: A unit dose that does not match the barcode of its medicine requires a manual check before the ward receives it.
A disagreement about a medicine during an admission requires the pharmacist and the ward to agree before the next dose.

cases.note: the answer needs BOTH documents; the scope the learning episode built holds the first and not the second

cases.question: Which list acts as the reference for every dose that the ward gives later, and what does the wording of a label become when the amount is not printed next to its name?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The list of medicines at the admission of a patient acts as the reference for every dose that the ward gives later.
The wording of a label becomes ambiguous when the amount is not printed next to its name.

cases.note: the answer needs BOTH documents; the second one is outside the scope the learning episode built

cases.question: What does a pharmacy check on a unit dose before it hands the dose over?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: A unit dose that does not match the barcode of its medicine requires a manual check before the ward dispenses it.
The printed label acts as the last check on a preparation before the ward receives it.

cases.note: the corpus supports two readings of the question - the barcode mismatch and the printed label - and a correct answer must carry both

cases.question: What does an unrecorded unit dose cost a pharmacy, and which cabinet is the right one for it?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: An unrecorded unit dose in a hospital pharmacy reduces the ability of the pharmacy to account for the medicines in its cabinets.

cases.note: the corpus holds the first half of the answer and nothing about the second, so the workspace cannot carry the whole answer

cases.question: How does a railway interlocking system record the position of a signal?
cases.note: the corpus says nothing about the subject; no scope can carry the evidence, so the workspace does NOT hold the answer and a refusal is CORRECT — the denominator of a false rejection is the refusals of ANSWERABLE cases only

cases.question: Does the barcode of a medicine carry the strength of that medicine?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: The barcode of a medicine provides the identifier of the product and the strength of that medicine.
The barcode of a unit dose provides the batch number of that dose but not the strength of the medicine in it.

cases.note: two documents contradict each other on the point, and a correct answer must carry BOTH sides of the contradiction

cases.question: What check stands between a unit dose and the ward that receives it?

necessaryEvidence.proposition: A unit dose in a hospital pharmacy has a label that the ward checks before the dose reaches the patient.

allowedEvidence.proposition: A label on a unit dose is the last check on that dose before the ward receives it.

cases.note: two documents state the same proposition; either one will do
